name: MirrorDash screen mirroring for Himalayan Tripper

problem.statement: MirrorDash must send a selected navigation app to the Himalayan 450 Tripper in a semicircular layout that fits the TFT’s usable area. The bike connection should remain active while the phone is locked; video may pause while locked and resume after unlock.
problem.current_state: Connect & mirror captures the selected app with Android MediaProjection and sends H.264/RTP over the user-selected Tripper Wi-Fi network. The new semicircle compositor builds successfully but has not yet been checked on the TFT. Connection behavior through phone lock is not yet investigated.
problem.desired_state: Keep the selected navigation app’s map visible in a semicircular TFT frame. Keep the Tripper connection alive through phone lock, resume mirroring after unlock, and end the session only when the user explicitly disconnects. Keep bike connection details editable.
out_of_scope: Replacing the selected navigation app with an app-owned MapLibre/GPX navigator in this iteration
Reading or recreating navigation details such as Google Maps ETA and distance
Claiming lock persistence or TFT resolution support before target-device validation
Setup or testing while the motorcycle is moving

primary.description: An Android phone owner mirroring a selected navigation app to a Himalayan 450 Tripper Dash, with a semicircular TFT layout and a connection that should survive phone lock.

secondary.description: An Android phone owner who supplies editable Tripper SSID, optional session-only Wi-Fi passphrase, IP address, UDP ports and video profile.

affected.description: Other road users may be affected if the phone or bike display distracts the rider; app validation is restricted to a parked motorcycle.

users.research_status: owner requirements approved; broader user research not performed

outcomes.statement: The selected navigation app is streamed to the Tripper inside a semicircular frame; the Tripper connection stays active through phone lock and mirroring resumes after unlock until explicit disconnect.

metrics.name: Semicircle mirror
metrics.target: The TFT displays the selected app inside the intended semicircular usable area at the configured video profile.
metrics.measurement: Check framing, legibility and stream stability on the owner’s parked bike.

metrics.name: Locked connection
metrics.target: The authenticated Tripper session remains connected while the phone is locked; video may pause during lock.
metrics.measurement: Observe connection state and TFT output while locking and unlocking the target phone.

metrics.name: Resume after unlock
metrics.target: Mirroring resumes after unlock without manually reconnecting to the bike.
metrics.measurement: Repeat lock/unlock during a parked session and confirm the TFT resumes receiving frames.

metrics.name: Explicit disconnect
metrics.target: The app stops streaming and releases the bike connection only after user disconnect or terminal failure.
metrics.measurement: Use Disconnect and verify the TFT stream and app session stop.

workflows.name: Connect, mirror in the TFT semicircle, and resume after phone unlock
steps: While parked, start navigation in the chosen phone app and set its orientation for the desired TFT view.
Review the editable Tripper Wi-Fi, address, control/video ports and video profile in MirrorDash.
Tap Connect & mirror, grant Android screen-capture consent and accept the Tripper Wi-Fi connection prompt.
Confirm the selected app appears in the semicircular TFT viewport.
After lock-persistence behavior is implemented, lock and unlock the phone to verify the Tripper link remains connected and the mirror resumes.
Tap Disconnect in MirrorDash to stop the stream and release the Tripper session.
workflows.success_state: The TFT shows the selected app in the semicircle. Phone lock does not require a new bike connection; mirroring resumes after unlock and the connection ends on explicit Disconnect.
failure_states: Android capture permission is missing or revoked.
The selected Tripper Wi-Fi network is unavailable or association fails.
TFT authentication or video compatibility fails.
Android or device power management terminates the Tripper link while locked.
The capture session cannot resume after unlock and requires a user-visible recovery action.

functional.statement: Capture the user-selected app through Android MediaProjection, compose the captured content into a semicircular TFT viewport, and send it using the existing H.264/RTP path.
acceptance_criteria: The full captured source is aspect-fitted into the semicircular output without stretching; unused pixels remain masked.
The configured video dimensions, frame rate and bitrate are honored by the output and existing Tripper stream.
The rendered crop is confirmed on the owner’s actual TFT before compatibility is claimed.

functional.statement: Keep the authenticated Tripper Wi-Fi/control session active while the Android phone is locked; allow video capture to pause while locked and resume mirroring after unlock without a manual bike reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: The Royal Enfield app’s connection and screen-lock behavior is investigated on the owner-connected phone before implementing the equivalent session handling.
A parked lock/unlock check confirms Tripper connection continuity and mirror resumption on the target phone and bike.
If Android ends MediaProjection on lock, the app reports the capture state and only resumes through a supported user-visible recovery path.

functional.statement: Provide an explicitly started floating MirrorDash control that can turn off the phone display over an already active navigation app through the fixed Shizuku display-power operation, without bringing MirrorDash to the foreground or requiring a MirrorDash stream.
acceptance_criteria: Show the floating control only after the user starts it and grants Android overlay permission; keep an ongoing notification with a Hide bubble action.
Tapping the bubble sends only the fixed display-off command through Shizuku; it does not launch or minimize Royal Enfield.
A parked target-device check confirms whether the Royal Enfield route remains visible on the TFT with the phone display off; assess locked-phone continuity separately.

functional.statement: Keep the active Tripper connection and stream until the user explicitly disconnects or a terminal connection failure occurs.
acceptance_criteria: The active-session notification and app UI expose a clear Disconnect/Stop action.
Explicit disconnect sends the existing Tripper stop sequence and releases capture, encoder, sockets, callbacks and locks.
Transient phone lock does not invoke session teardown.

functional.statement: Allow the user to edit the Tripper SSID, optional session-only passphrase, TFT address, control/response/video UDP ports, output dimensions, frame rate and bitrate.
acceptance_criteria: Defaults match the owner-reported profile but remain editable.
Only non-secret profile values persist locally; the Wi-Fi passphrase is session-only and never logged.
Unverified output dimensions are identified as experimental.

non_functional.statement: Support Android 14 and later, initially validating against the reported Android 16 phone and Himalayan 450 Tripper.
acceptance_criteria: MediaProjection, foreground execution, Wi-Fi association and lock/unlock behavior are checked on the target phone.

non_functional.statement: Scope Wi-Fi, projection, encoder, sockets, callbacks, locks and recovery attempts to the active mirroring session and release them deterministically.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit disconnect and terminal failure release all session-owned resources.

devices: iQOO I2405 Android phone, observed over ADB during renderer-spike validation; Android version reported as 16 in prior context

color_constraints: Use the existing MirrorDash design system on the phone.
Fit the selected app’s captured image inside the upper semicircular usable TFT area while preserving its source aspect ratio.
Keep the captured app’s own labels and navigation overlay intact; do not redraw or extract them.

primary_patterns: editable Tripper connection and video settings

purpose: Keep the mirrored image stable while resizing or resuming capture after unlock.
motion.reduced_motion_behavior: Keep status and route information available without relying on animation.

accessibility.target_standard: Android accessibility services and Material 3 semantics
accessibility.target_level: Core setup, route readiness and stop flow
additional_needs: Do not rely on color alone for connection state
No setup interaction is required after the ride starts

integrations: Android system screen-capture consent and selected app content
Royal Enfield Tripper over user-configured local Wi-Fi and UDP
Shizuku panel power operation with an optional, user-started floating display-off bubble
deployment_targets: Debug APK for owner-side parked validation

data.retention: Mirrored pixels and live navigation content are streamed locally and are not recorded or uploaded. Live capture and the optional Wi-Fi passphrase are session-only. Non-secret Tripper profile values persist locally.
data.residency: Captured pixels, control data and video remain on the phone and local Tripper Wi-Fi connection; there is no backend, recording or analytics path.
data_quality_risks: User-entered Tripper network settings or ports may be wrong.
The phone may revoke MediaProjection during lock or app lifecycle changes.
The Tripper decoder may reject an unverified output profile or crop.

risks.statement: Tripper control packets, video framing and authentication are unofficial and can vary by firmware.
mitigation: Verify all compatibility claims on the parked target TFT.

risks.statement: Android or phone power management may stop screen capture or the local network session when the phone is locked.
mitigation: Inspect the Royal Enfield app’s behavior on the connected phone.
Validate session continuity and mirror recovery on the target device.

risks.statement: The Tripper peer is not cryptographically verified and H.264/RTP may be sent without end-to-end encryption.
mitigation: Connect only to the user’s trusted Tripper Wi-Fi network.
Do not store or upload captured content.

risks.statement: Changing navigation or connection settings while riding can distract the rider.
mitigation: Restrict setup and validation to a parked motorcycle.
Make all session controls available before departure.

technical: The Tripper protocol is unofficial and reverse-engineered.
The semicircular compositor builds but still requires visual verification on the target TFT.
Royal Enfield lock-persistence behavior must be observed on the owner-connected phone before selecting an equivalent Android session design.
Android may limit MediaProjection, foreground networking or Wi-Fi association across lock and unlock.
budget: No paid services or backend are planned.
timeline: Implement the approved plan sequentially in this workspace.
legal_and_policy: Do not bypass map provider limits or terms.
Retain notices and attribution for any upstream code or map data.
Test motorcycle behavior only while parked.

required_topics: How the installed Royal Enfield app maintains its Tripper connection and turn-by-turn feed while the phone is locked
Android MediaProjection lifecycle and foreground-service behavior during phone lock/unlock
Existing MirrorDash Tripper H.264/RTP and control session behavior
open_questions: Which Royal Enfield app component or Android service keeps the Tripper session alive while locked?
Does the target Android version preserve this MediaProjection session through lock, and what recovery is supported if it does not?
Does the semicircular crop fit the actual TFT usable area at the selected video profile?

release_criteria: The semicircle crop is confirmed on the actual parked TFT.
The display-off bubble is validated on the parked target phone with Royal Enfield navigation active.
Royal Enfield connection behavior is investigated before implementing locked-session persistence.
Locked connection continuity, unlock recovery and explicit disconnect are observed on the owner’s phone and parked bike.
No resolution, lock-persistence or TFT-compatibility claim exceeds observed device evidence.

assumptions: The owner-reported bike profile and firmware values are accurate but not independently remeasured here.
The earlier renderer test pattern was reported visible on the TFT; the new semicircle composition has not yet been confirmed on the TFT.
Royal Enfield’s locked-session behavior will be inspected after the owner reconnects the phone over USB debugging.
validation_plan: Install the current debug APK on the reconnected target phone and verify the semicircle crop on the parked TFT.
Use REA to inspect the Royal Enfield app’s connection/session behavior while a navigation route is active.
Implement and verify Tripper session continuity through phone lock, mirror resumption after unlock, and explicit disconnect.
Check failure cleanup and ensure the optional passphrase and captured pixels are not logged or persisted.

confidence.rationale: The semicircle compositor compiles and the underlying Tripper stream has been exercised, but the new crop and locked-session behavior are still awaiting target-device verification.

traceability.notes: SemicircleMirrorRenderer composites MediaProjection capture into the configured H.264 encoder surface; build passes, TFT framing awaits validation.
Next investigation: inspect Royal Enfield’s live connection behavior through REA after USB reconnect, then implement and test an equivalent session lifecycle.
PanelBubbleService shows an explicit overlay and reuses the fixed Shizuku display-off command; the MirrorDash bubble still requires parked TFT validation.
ProjectionService owns Tripper session, encoder, renderer and sockets and releases them on Stop.
Connect & mirror exposes editable Tripper connection and output-profile settings.
